questions.knowledge_point: Adding Rational Expressions in One Variable With Common Factors in the Denominators
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to add the following fractions:

$$
p+q=\frac{6y}{5(1-2y)}+\frac{9-4y}{1-2y}
$$

In order to add the two fractions, we need them to have a common denominator. Here, we can put both fractions over a common denominator of $5(1-2y)$ if we multiply the top and bottom of the second fraction by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6y}{5(1-2y)}+\frac{9-4y}{1-2y} & = \\ \frac{6y}{5(1-2y)}+\frac{5}{5}\cdot \frac{9-4y}{1-2y} & = \\ \frac{6y}{5(1-2y)}+\frac{5(9-4y)}{5(1-2y)} & = \\ \frac{6y+5(9-4y)}{5(1-2y)} & = \\ \frac{6y+45-20y}{5(1-2y)} & = \\ \frac{-14y+45}{5(1-2y)} & \end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Adding Rational Expressions in Multiple Variables With Common Factors in the Denominators
questions.worked_solution:
In order to add the two fractions, we need them to have a common denominator. Here, we can put both fractions over a common denominator of $a(b-3)$ if we multiply the top and bottom of the second fraction by $b-3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{a(b-3)}+\frac{1}{a} & = \\ \frac{3}{a(b-3)}+\frac{b-3}{b-3}\cdot \frac{1}{a} & = \\ \frac{3}{a(b-3)}+\frac{b-3}{a(b-3)} & = \\ \frac{3+b-3}{a(b-3)} & = \\ \frac{b}{a(b-3)} & \end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Adding Rational Expressions in Multiple Variables With Common Factors in the Denominators
questions.worked_solution:
In order to add the two fractions, we need them to have a common denominator. Here, we can put both fractions over a common denominator of $2(k+3t)$ if we multiply the top and bottom of the second fraction by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3t}{2(k+3t)}+\frac{k}{k+3t} & = \\ \frac{3t}{2(k+3t)}+\frac{2}{2}\cdot \frac{k}{k+3t} & = \\ \frac{3t}{2(k+3t)}+\frac{2k}{2(k+3t)} & = \\ \frac{3t+2k}{2(k+3t)} & \end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Adding Rational Expressions in One Variable With Common Factors in the Denominators
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to subtract the following fractions:

$$
b-c=\frac{5n+3}{n-2}-\frac{2n-1}{2-n}
$$

In order to subtract the two fractions, we need them to have a common denominator. Here, we can put both fractions over a common denominator of $n-2$ if we multiply the top and bottom of the second fraction by $-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5n+3}{n-2}-\frac{2n-1}{2-n} & = \\ \frac{5n+3}{n-2}-\frac{(-1)}{(-1)}\cdot \frac{2n-1}{2-n} & = \\ \frac{5n+3}{n-2}-\frac{-2n+1}{n-2} & = \\ \frac{(5n+3)-(-2n+1)}{n-2} & = \\ \frac{5n+3+2n-1}{n-2} & = \\ \frac{7n+2}{n-2} & \end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Adding Rational Expressions in Multiple Variables With Common Factors in the Denominators
questions.worked_solution:
In order to subtract the two fractions, we need them to have a common denominator. Here, we can put both fractions over a common denominator of $c(5d+1)$ if we multiply the top and bottom of the second fraction by $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{c(5d+1)}-\frac{5}{5d+1} & = \\ \frac{3}{c(5d+1)}-\frac{c}{c}\cdot \frac{5}{5d+1} & = \\ \frac{3}{c(5d+1)}-\frac{5c}{c(5d+1)} & = \\ \frac{3-5c}{c(5d+1)} & \end{aligned}
$$
